tagline: The Post Road past Madison's green and a giant's rock.
intro: Through Madison US 1 still goes by its old name, the Boston Post Road, and the scenic part runs two and a third miles from Neck Road to Lover's Lane. Interstate 95 has taken over the through traffic, and US 1 is mostly a local business route now.

The green came first. In 1705 it was laid out around the meeting house of a new parish called East Guilford, the village grew up around it, and when Madison became a town in 1826 the green became its center.

moments.title: Shelley House
moments.text: At 248 Boston Post Road a late 17th-century stone ender grew room by room into a saltbox, and of its first owners little is known beyond the name Shelley.

moments.title: Madison Green
moments.text: The 1838 First Congregational Church owns the green it faces, with a row of 18th- and 19th-century houses across the Post Road and the Deacon John Grave House of 1681 just east.

moments.title: Samson Rock
moments.text: Algonquin legend says the giant Odziozo dropped this boulder as he flung the earth of Tuxis Pond out to sea, and it now sits between two shopping centers and a parking lot.
